outcome: Type of BPBP (Erb's palsy vs. Klumpke's palsy)
cohort: 320 infants diagnosed with brachial plexus birth palsy at the Volta Regional Hospital
finding: The prevalence of brachial plexus birth palsy was 14.7%, and Erb's palsy was the most common type, accounting for 93.6% of cases.
mod_finding: The study found that 93.6% of brachial plexus birth palsy cases were Erb's palsy, but it did not specifically investigate the relationship between mode of delivery and brachial plexus birth palsy.
